zh.title: 蕭美琴提出三大支柱鞏固臺灣無人機供應鏈亞洲中心地位
zh.summary: 蕭美琴提出三項無人機產業支柱，盼鞏固臺灣供應鏈地位
body: 副總統蕭美琴在臺灣無人機國際論壇暨無人機國際學院開幕活動致詞，提出鞏固臺灣作為無人機民主供應鏈亞洲中心的三大支柱。她表示，臺灣的發展方向包括建立可信賴的非紅供應鏈、推動邊緣人工智慧與軟體定義創新，以及加強國際合作與無人機外交。
在供應鏈方面，蕭美琴表示，臺灣致力打造100%非紅供應鏈，並以微處理器、飛行控制器等符合網路安全和運作完整性標準為目標。她提到，民主國家需要安全的替代方案。這是她所列出的第一項支柱。
第二項支柱是邊緣人工智慧和軟體定義創新。蕭美琴指出，軟體已成為無人機技術的關鍵差異化因素，臺灣正把邊緣人工智慧融入自主平臺，用於即時決策、感測器融合，以及在無GPS環境下導航。她並表示，臺灣的半導體和人工智慧生態系可為合作夥伴提供下一代平臺。
第三項支柱是國際合作。蕭美琴表示，臺灣無法獨自建構供應鏈，合作方式包括聯合研發、技術轉移、合作生產和採購。她說，能大規模生產無人系統的國家不多，臺灣在研發、OEM和量產方面的優勢，使其成為理想的合作生產夥伴。
蕭美琴並表示，今年上半年臺灣無人機出口額已超過去年全年。她舉例，今年6月出訪帛琉期間，外交部捐贈4架用於海上巡邏和救難的無人機。

en.title: Hsiao Sets Out Three Pillars to Strengthen Taiwan’s Drone Supply Chain
en.summary: Vice President Hsiao outlines three pillars to strengthen Taiwan’s role in the drone supply chain.
body: Taiwan Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim set out three pillars for strengthening Taiwan’s position as an Asian hub for a democratic drone supply chain. She delivered the remarks at the Taiwan International Drone Forum and the opening event for the Global UAV Academy. The pillars she described are a trusted non-China supply chain, edge AI and software-defined innovation, and international cooperation and drone diplomacy.

On supply chains, Hsiao said Taiwan is working to build a 100% trusted, non-China supply chain. She said this would ensure that components including microprocessors and flight controllers meet high standards for cybersecurity and operational integrity. Hsiao also said democratic countries need secure alternatives to supply-chain dependence and backdoors.

The second pillar, edge AI and software-defined innovation, reflects what Hsiao described as software’s role as a key differentiator in drone technology. She said Taiwan is integrating edge AI into autonomous platforms for real-time decision-making, sensor fusion and navigation in GPS-denied environments. She added that Taiwan’s semiconductor and AI ecosystems can provide next-generation platforms for partners.

The third pillar is international cooperation. Hsiao said Taiwan cannot build a supply chain alone and cited joint research and development, technology transfer, co-production and procurement as areas for global cooperation. She said few countries can produce unmanned systems at scale, and described Taiwan’s strengths in research and development, OEM and mass production as making it an ideal co-production partner.

Hsiao said Taiwan’s drone exports in the first half of this year had already exceeded the total for the previous year. As an example of cooperation, she cited a donation by Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs of four drones for maritime patrol and rescue during a visit to Palau in June.
